mainTopic: Explaining the dispute over judges for מוציא שם רע, then רב יוסף and רבא on lying witnesses and on testimony that involves the witness himself.
overview: The amud begins at the end of רבי's view, quoted from a משנה in מכות: a relative who saw a crime but did not act as a witness does not cancel the other witnesses. Otherwise, what could two brothers and an outsider do if they saw a murder? This was one way to explain the dispute in our משנה about how many judges a מוציא שם רע case needs. The גמרא then gives two more explanations. One ties the dispute to רבי יוסי's rule that the witnesses themselves must give the warning (התראה). The other ties it to whether a contradiction in small details (בדיקות) cancels testimony, as in the story of בן זכאי and the fig stems. Next, רב יוסף teaches about rounds of עדים זוממין in a husband's adultery claim. Lying witnesses usually get only the bigger punishment, but they get both death and payment when the harms were aimed at different people. רב יוסף also rules that a man forced into a forbidden act may testify against the sinner, but one who says he consented is a רשע and cannot testify. רבא disagrees, since a person is a relative to himself and cannot make himself a רשע. The amud ends as רבא begins another teaching, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What would two brothers and a third person do?
steps.stepSummary: The quoted source ends with רבי's own argument against רבי יוסי: if merely seeing a crime together with a relative cancelled testimony, many murders could never be judged.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that were not so, what should two brothers and one other person do if they saw someone kill a person?
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the quote of רבי's view, which the גמרא brought just before this section. רבי asks a pointed question to show that a person becomes a witness only if he chooses to act as one, and does not become one just by seeing something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two brothers cannot testify together, because relatives are disqualified as a pair. If everyone who saw the crime automatically counted as a witness, the brothers would cancel the whole group, and the murderer could never be judged. So one brother can step back, and the other brother joins the outsider to form a valid pair of witnesses. This is רבי's reason that a relative who did not take part, for example by not warning the sinner, does not cancel the others.

keyTerms.meaning: Two brothers, who are relatives and so cannot serve as witnesses together
Killed a person, meaning committed murder
What should they do? This is a question that shows the other view leads to a bad result

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the closing point of the previous explanation, which deals with relatives among the witnesses, and it continues from the text just before this section.

phrases.english: What should two brothers and one other person do,
who saw someone kill a person?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of רבי's view (against רבי יוסי, on relatives who saw the crime but did not warn) that the גמרא cited just before this section. This is רבי's own argument that the other view leads to a bad result.
steps.raayaObject: The view that a relative who did not join in the testimony does not cancel the other witnesses.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: otherwise no murder seen by two brothers and one outsider could ever be judged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person becomes a witness only by actively joining the testimony, not simply by seeing the event.

steps.title: Another explanation: others warned her, not the witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a new way to explain the משנה's dispute: the case is one where other people warned the woman, and the witnesses themselves did not warn her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say instead: the case is one where others warned her, and the witnesses did not warn her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second, different explanation of why רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree. It describes the exact case being discussed, and this sets up the next step, which says which earlier dispute this depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can be put to death by a court only if he was warned (התראה) before sinning. Here a warning was given, but it came from people other than the witnesses. The question is whether that kind of warning is good enough to make this a capital case.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say. This introduces another possible explanation
They warned. This is from הַתְרָאָה, the warning required before a court can punish
Others, meaning people who are not the witnesses

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
for example, where others warned her,
phrases.notes: 'Her' is the betrothed woman accused of being unfaithful in the מוציא שם רע case.

phrases.english: and the witnesses did not warn her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא כְּגוֹן שֶׁהִתְרוּ בָּהּ אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside the relatives explanation and offers a new case to explain the משנה's dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the case: the dispute is placed in a specific situation where only outsiders gave the warning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute in the משנה could only be explained through the relatives case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute could instead be about a case where non-witnesses gave the warning.

steps.title: The dispute depends on רבי יוסי and the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects this case to a known dispute: רבי יוסי holds that the witnesses themselves must give the warning, based on the פסוק 'על פי שנים עדים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they disagree on the same point as רבי יוסי and the חכמים. As we learned: רבי יוסי says, a person is never put to death unless the mouths of his two witnesses warn him, as it says: 'At the mouth of two witnesses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows which earlier dispute the משנה depends on: רבי יוסי's rule that only the witnesses can give the warning. It quotes his statement and the פסוק he learns it from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי, a warning from others does not count, so the woman cannot be put to death. That means three judges are enough, which is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים disagree with רבי יוסי and accept a warning from others, so she could face death, and twenty-three judges are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And they disagree
About the same issue as an earlier dispute
The mouths of his two witnesses
Warning him

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the number of judges depends on one question: could this woman actually be put to death? That in turn depends on who is allowed to give the warning.

phrases.english: And they disagree on the issue disputed by Rabbi Yosei and the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי מאיר and the חכמים from our משנה.

phrases.english: as we learned: Rabbi Yosei says,
he is never executed

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ פִּי שְׁנֵי עֵדָיו מַתְרִין בּוֹ,
phrases.english: unless the mouths of his two witnesses warn him,
as it is said: "At the mouth of two witnesses."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the known dispute behind the case described in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's dispute can be explained as a dispute over whether a warning from non-witnesses counts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מכות: רבי יוסי requires the witnesses themselves to give the warning, learned from 'על פי שנים עדים'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: a person is not executed unless his two witnesses themselves warned him.

steps.title: A third explanation: contradiction in small details only
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another explanation: the witnesses contradicted each other in the minor-detail questions (בדיקות) but not in the main questions (חקירות).
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say instead: the case is one where the witnesses were contradicted in the בדיקות, but not in the חקירות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third, different explanation of the משנה's dispute. It describes the case first, and this sets up the next step, which names the earlier dispute behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Judges question witnesses in two ways. חקירות are the main questions, about when and where the event happened. בדיקות are the side-detail questions. Here the witnesses agreed on the main facts but clashed on small details, and the question is whether that cancels their testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: Were contradicted, meaning the witnesses' answers clashed
Questions about side details of the event
The main questions, about time and place

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up חקירות and בדיקות. חקירות are the basic time-and-place questions. בדיקות are the smaller detail questions.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
for example, where they were contradicted in the examinations,
but were not contradicted in the interrogations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers yet another case to explain the משנה, alongside the warning explanation of steps 2 and 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the case: the dispute is placed in a situation where the witnesses clashed only on minor details.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute could only be explained through the cases already offered: relatives among the witnesses, or who gave the warning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute could instead be about whether a contradiction in בדיקות cancels testimony.

steps.title: The dispute depends on בן זכאי and the fig stems
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ties this case to the dispute between בן זכאי and the חכמים, quoting the story in which בן זכאי questioned witnesses about the stems of figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they disagree on the same point as בן זכאי and the חכמים. As we learned: there was an incident, and בן זכאי examined the witnesses about the stems of figs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the earlier dispute behind the third explanation. בן זכאי checked the witnesses on tiny details like fig stems, and this shows he treated small-detail questions seriously.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בן זכאי's approach, a contradiction in small details like fig stems cancels the testimony. So the woman cannot be put to death, and three judges are enough, which fits רבי מאיר. The חכמים do not cancel testimony over contradictions in בדיקות, so she could face death, and twenty-three judges are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Ben Zakkai, the judge in the story who questioned witnesses about fine details
An incident, meaning a real event that happened
Stems of figs

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא gave several ways to explain why רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree on the number of judges for מוציא שם רע. In each one, the real question is whether the woman could actually face the death penalty. That turns on relatives among the witnesses, on who gave the warning, or on contradictions in בדיקות.

phrases.english: And they disagree on the issue disputed by Ben Zakkai and the Rabbis,
as we learned: There was an incident, and Ben Zakkai examined the witnesses
about the stems of figs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the known dispute behind the case described in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's dispute can be explained as a dispute over whether contradictions in בדיקות cancel testimony.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about בן זכאי questioning witnesses about the stems of figs.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The disagreement over the number of judges can be explained through the dispute of בן זכאי and the חכמים on whether contradictions in בדיקות cancel testimony.

steps.title: The husband's lying witnesses are executed but pay no money
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that if the father proves the husband's witnesses are עדים זוממין, they are executed and do not pay money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: A husband brought witnesses that his wife committed adultery. Then her father brought witnesses who proved the husband's witnesses were זוממין. The husband's witnesses are executed, and they do not pay money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רב יוסף about a husband who accuses his wife of adultery. Here the husband's own witnesses are caught lying through הזמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's witnesses tried to get the woman executed, and their lie would also have cost her money. Since they receive the death penalty, the bigger punishment covers everything, and they pay nothing on top of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Proving witnesses false by showing they were somewhere else at the time they claimed to see the event
Plotting witnesses who were caught through הזמה; they receive the punishment they tried to bring on the accused
They are executed
They pay money

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
If the husband brought witnesses that she committed adultery,
and the father brought witnesses
and they proved the husband's witnesses to be זוממין,
phrases.notes: The father is the wife's father. He is defending his daughter.

phrases.english: the husband's witnesses are executed
and they do not pay money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הֵבִיא הַבַּעַל עֵדִים שֶׁזִּינְּתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching of רב יוסף about the adultery and מוציא שם רע case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the husband's witnesses are proven זוממין, they are executed but are exempt from paying money.

steps.title: The father's lying witnesses are executed and also pay
steps.stepSummary: If the husband then proves the father's witnesses are זוממין, those witnesses are executed and also pay money, because the money and the death penalty are owed to different people.
steps.simpleTranslation: The husband came back and brought new witnesses, who proved the father's witnesses were זוממין. The father's witnesses are executed, and they also pay money. The money is for this one (the husband), and the lives are for that one (the first set of witnesses).
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף continues the same case one more round. Now the father's witnesses are caught lying, and they get both punishments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's witnesses tried to get the husband's witnesses killed, so they are executed. They also tried to make the husband pay a fine, so they pay him. Since the two harms were aimed at different people, the death penalty does not cancel the payment, unlike step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back and did it again
Money for this one
Lives for that one

steps.whatToRemember: One harm aimed at one person brings only the bigger punishment (step 6). Two harms aimed at two different people bring both punishments (step 7).
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the father's witnesses are executed for trying to kill the wife. They are executed because they tried to get the husband's witnesses killed.

phrases.english: If the husband went back and brought witnesses,
and they proved the father's witnesses to be זוממין,
the father's witnesses are executed,
and they pay money.
Money for this one, and lives for that one.
phrases.notes: The money goes to the husband. The death penalty is for trying to kill the husband's witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 6 with a second round of הזמה and contrasts the outcome
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The father's witnesses who are proven זוממין receive both death and payment, since the money and the death penalty relate to different victims.

steps.title: A victim of forced sin may testify against the sinner
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that a man who testifies that another man forced him into a forbidden relationship can join with one more witness to have the sinner executed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: If a man testifies, "So-and-so lay with me against my will," he and another witness join together to have him executed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from רב יוסף. It is about a man testifying about a sin that was done to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he was forced, he did nothing wrong, so he is still a kosher witness. Being the victim does not disqualify him, and he counts as one of the two witnesses needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Lay with him in a forbidden way (the איסור of משכב זכר)
Against his will, by force
They join together to make a pair of witnesses

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
If one testifies, "So-and-so lay with him against his will,"
phrases.notes: "Him" is the witness himself. He is telling the court what was done to him.

phrases.english: he and another join together to execute him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: פְּלוֹנִי רְבָעוֹ לְאוֹנְסוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate ruling of רב יוסף about one witness's testimony
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who was forced may testify against the one who forced him and combine with another witness for execution.

steps.title: A willing participant is wicked and cannot testify
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף continues: if the man says he consented, he is calling himself a רשע, and a רשע may not testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he says, "with my consent," he is wicked, and the תורה said: "Do not put a wicked one as a witness."
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the other side of his ruling. If the witness admits he went along willingly, his testimony is thrown out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying he consented, the witness admits he also sinned. In רב יוסף's view, this makes him a רשע, and the פסוק disqualifies a רשע from being a witness, so his whole testimony fails.

keyTerms.meaning: With his consent, willingly
A wicked person, who may not serve as a witness
"Do not put a wicked one as a witness" (the פסוק that disqualifies a רשע)

phrases.english: If he says, "With his consent,"
he is wicked,
and the Torah said:
"Do not put a wicked one as a witness."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of רב יוסף's ruling, contrasting willing with forced
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A witness who admits he consented is a רשע and is disqualified, based on אל תשת רשע עד.

steps.title: רבא: a person cannot make himself wicked
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רב יוסף: a person is a relative to himself, so his words against himself are not accepted, and he cannot make himself a רשע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A person is a relative to himself, and a person cannot make himself wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא argues with רב יוסף's second ruling about the willing participant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A relative cannot testify about someone, and every person counts as his own closest relative. So the witness's words against himself are simply ignored, and he is not considered a רשע. His testimony about the other man is still accepted, and he can join with another witness, just like the forced case.

keyTerms.meaning: A person is a relative to himself, so he cannot testify about himself
A person cannot make himself wicked through his own words

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף says the willing participant is disqualified as a רשע. רבא says we ignore the part about himself and still accept his testimony against the other man.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the man is believed that he sinned. He is saying the court does not listen to that part at all, so it cannot disqualify him.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's idea, that we can accept one part of a person's testimony and ignore the part about himself, is a key tool in the laws of testimony.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A person is a relative to himself,
phrases.notes: Relatives can't testify, and nobody is closer to you than you, so you can't testify about yourself.

phrases.english: and a person cannot make himself wicked.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אָדָם קָרוֹב אֵצֶל עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב יוסף's ruling in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A witness's admission about himself is ignored, since a person is a relative to himself. He is not a רשע, and his testimony against the other man stands.

steps.title: רבא introduces a new teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new statement in the name of רבא. The content of the statement follows in the next lines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by introducing a new statement from רבא. The ruling itself has not been said yet; it comes right after these words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10, רבא taught that a person is a relative to himself, so his words against himself are not accepted. These opening words tell us that רבא is about to say more. When the actual ruling comes, check how it connects to that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: A statement or ruling given by an אמורא in his own name.

phrases.english: Rava says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Right after his disagreement with רב יוסף in Step 10, רבא is introduced again as the speaker of a new teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the attribution appears on this amud. רבא's ruling comes on the next amud.
